strings.title: Elevens and Twelves
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Elevens are ten groups plus one more group; twelves are ten groups plus two more groups.
strings.keywords: groups of, tens and ones, split a factor, ten and one more, ten and two more
watchFor: Treating 11 × 12 like the 11 pattern for one-digit numbers (writing 1212): ask "Is it 10 twelves plus one twelve?"
Forgetting the extra groups: ask "What's left after the 10 groups?"
Adding 2 instead of 2 groups: ask "Two more of what?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did 10 groups help every time?" Land: 11 × n is 10 × n plus n; 12 × n is 10 × n plus 2 × n. Split the 11 or 12 into 10 and a little more.

problems.notes: Look for: 40 + 4. Ask: "How is 11 like 10?" Word choice: "10 groups and 1 more group". Model: area 10+1 x 4
Look for: 70 + 7. Ask: "What's the pattern?" Model: area 10+1 x 7
Look for: 120 + 12. Ask: "Does the pattern still work?" Model: area 10+1 x 12

responses.say: 10 twelves is 120, one more twelve is 132.
responses.tip: The repeating-digit pattern stops here. Ask: why?
Stretched the pattern. Ask: is 10 × 12 + 12 equal to 1212?

problems.notes: Look for: 50 + 10. Ask: "What is 2 more groups of 5?" Model: area 10+2 x 5
Look for: 60 + 12. Ask: "How does 12 × 5 help?" Model: area 10+2 x 6

responses.tip: Added 2, not 2 groups of 6. Ask: two more of what?

problems.notes: Look for: 80 + 16. Ask: "Which way do you split the 12?" Model: area 10+2 x 8

responses.tip: Doubling. Also a fact you know.

problems.notes: Look for: 120 + 24. Ask: "Which earlier problem helps?" Model: area 10+2 x 12
